stewart_read: This is the excessive_contact_complaint protocol — a real operational friction, not a sales objection — and the rep should resolve it early via action, not defense.
coaching_implication: Rep should have addressed this immediately with a concrete fix ('let me pull you out of the dialer right now') instead of pivoting straight to the pitch.

quote: And now I've had five more people call me.
stewart_read: Second touch on the same contact-frequency complaint; rep offers a scheduling fix but still doesn't apologize or explain why the promised callback never happened.
coaching_implication: Acknowledge the broken promise specifically ('someone was supposed to follow up and didn't — that's on us') before pivoting to scheduling.

quote: sorry for all the phone calls. I know our dialer is kind of aggressive
stewart_read: Third touch: the apology finally lands, but only after the appointment is locked — sequencing suggests it was a closing courtesy, not genuine resolution.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as strategic — rep chose to book first while customer was cooperative, then close with goodwill. But nothing in the transcript shows this was deliberate sequencing rather than just skipping it until the end.
coaching_implication: Move the apology to the front of the call; trust repair before ask lands better than trust repair after ask.

quote: Well, last year. It depends what address, I guess.
stewart_read: Customer signals ambiguity/multiple properties or uncertainty about the prior design; rep confirms the address but never asks what the customer thought of the design or whether they're still interested in it.
coaching_implication: Should have asked 'what did you think of the design when you saw it?' to re-anchor interest before jumping to scheduling.

quote: it looks like we were reaching out because we had put together a solar design for your home.
stewart_read: Rep mentions an existing solar design — a strong anchor (customer already has a number/design on file) — but never reflects it back as a hook ('let's get you back in front of those numbers').
coaching_implication: Use the existing design as forward-pull: 'you're already ahead of most people — you've got a design ready to review' would have re-engaged interest instead of just logistics.

quote: And and we'll just need a text beforehand just to reconfirm that appointment.
stewart_read: Button-up is only partially run — no restated day/time recap with a verbal 'is that fair?' handshake, no one-hour block or no-driving instruction.
coaching_implication: Complete the full button-up: restate day+time, one-hour block, no-driving/computer instruction, and the fairness handshake to lock show-rate.
